feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for senior digital communications roles: the progression at NACo is clear, the scope is substantial, and the profile aligns well with strategy/operations leadership. Writing is polished overall, but the document is somewhat dense and repetitive, with a few style/grammar inconsistencies that reduce sharpness.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear career progression and credibility: multiple promotions at one organization show growth, trust, and increasing leadership scope.  
- Good impact signals: 10,000+ page migration, 3.5 million annual page views, 50+ publishers, and analytics stack details add substance.  
- Strong positioning for modern digital leadership: combines strategy, CMS/platform work, analytics, governance, and multimedia.

1. Top improvements  
- Tighten repetition and structure: “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT” overlap heavily; consolidate to save space and improve scannability.  
- Add more outcome-focused metrics beyond activity descriptions, especially for the freelance role and earlier NACo roles (e.g., engagement, efficiency, revenue, adoption, campaign results).  
- Fix minor language/style issues: “12 years experience” should be “12 years’ experience” or “more than 12 years of experience”; maintain consistent serial comma usage (“web, email, social, and multimedia” vs “web, content, email, social media, and multimedia”); “A2/Learning” is stylistically awkward—use “French (A2, currently learning).”
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible summary with clear positioning, but it reads slightly generic and repeats themes covered in Core Competencies and Topline Skills. Tightening the language and adding a sharper leadership/value angle would improve impact.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Change “more than 12 years experience” to “12+ years of experience” for cleaner, more modern phrasing.
- Lead with your strongest differentiators: digital strategy leadership, platform modernization, and mission-driven/public-sector communications.
- Replace broad phrases like “web, content, email, social media, and multimedia programs” with “multi-channel digital communications” to reduce listiness.
- Suggested rewrite: Digital communications and strategy leader with 12+ years of experience driving multi-channel communications, platform modernization, and content operations for mission-driven organizations. Brings deep expertise in digital strategy, editorial workflow design, and cross-functional stakeholder coordination, with a strong track record translating technical and policy issues into clear, audience-focused content.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-channel communications,” “platform modernization,” and “stakeholder coordination” are repeated in Core Competencies/Topline Skills.
- “Mission-driven organizations” and advocacy/policy messaging also recur in experience bullets; keep the intro high-level.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block overlaps heavily with the header and Topline Skills. It would be more effective if tightened to emphasize higher-level strengths rather than repeating detailed skill categories listed elsewhere.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Replace broad or repetitive phrases with sharper, leadership-level terms: “Enterprise digital strategy,” “CMS modernization,” “Editorial governance,” “Analytics & insight reporting.”
- Standardize wording for parallel structure; e.g., use noun phrases consistently and change “Multi-channel communication” to “Multi-channel communications.”
- Prioritize the most marketable, recent capabilities tied to current roles: digital transformation, web platform leadership, analytics, governance, and AI-enabled search/content systems.
- Possible rewrite: Enterprise digital strategy & transformation • Multi-channel communications leadership • Web platform & CMS modernization • Editorial governance & workflow design • Analytics, reporting & optimization • Content systems architecture • Cross-functional stakeholder coordination • Advocacy & policy communications • Multimedia & live event production

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Significant overlap with the header (“cross-channel communications,” “platform modernization,” “workflows and systems”).
- Also overlaps with Topline Skills; avoid listing tools or sub-skills already covered there.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: Freelance (full-time engagement)
items.content:
Support a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, current role with clear scope and good technical depth, but it reads as a task list. Tighten it around outcomes, scale, and 2–3 signature contributions so it feels distinct from the NACo roles below.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a sharper positioning line: “Embedded as a full-time strategic communications consultant for a U.S. national membership organization, leading digital platform improvement, campaign delivery, and content operations.”
- Consolidate overlapping bullets into 4–5 impact-led bullets; start with strong verbs like “Modernized,” “Built,” “Led,” “Advised.”
- Add measurable context wherever possible: number of sites/pages/users, campaign launches, toolkit downloads, publishing teams supported, workflow time saved, search/discovery improvements.
- Example rewrite: “Led an AI-enabled search initiative across legislative/member content, defining retrieval strategy, structured content workflows, and discovery UX to improve findability of complex policy resources.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Governance, workflows, analytics” overlaps with the 2022–2024 Director role; emphasize consulting/embedded delivery and newer AI-search work.
- Drupal microsites and storytelling also overlap with Recent Projects; keep this entry higher-level and let the footer carry examples.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with good scale metrics; it should be tightened to foreground enterprise ownership and clearer outcomes. Emphasize what changed under your leadership, not just what you oversaw.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a sharper summary: “Directed enterprise digital communications strategy, platforms, analytics, governance, and budget for NACo’s web, email, social, and video ecosystem.”
- Rewrite bullets to lead with outcomes: “Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page Drupal website serving 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Add measurable impact where missing: growth in email/social engagement, reporting speed, production cost savings from the studio, or efficiency gains from governance/publishing standards.
- Combine lower-value bullets for concision: merge analytics + governance into one operational-improvement bullet if space is tight.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the earlier Associate Communications Director role; keep this entry focused on enterprise leadership, modernization, and infrastructure.
- Video studio/buildout may partially overlap with older multimedia bullets; frame it here as capacity-building and organizational scale.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this item is too close to the adjacent NACo roles and reads more like responsibilities than achievements. Sharpen it around scope, channel ownership, and outcomes that set up the promotion to Director.

Suggested edit:
- Open with progression + scope: “Promoted to lead NACo’s day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social and video, coordinating editorial and advocacy messaging across teams.”
- Tighten bullets to 3–4 high-value points: newsletter ownership, launch/growth of weekly advocacy video, cross-functional editorial planning, publishing workflow improvements.
- Add measurable outcomes where possible: subscriber counts, open/click rates, video cadence/views, turnaround time, number of teams/stakeholders coordinated.
- Use stronger verbs: “owned,” “launched/scaled,” “standardized,” “streamlined,” “coordinated.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Weekly advocacy video update” overlaps with both the earlier NACo role and the footer project; emphasize that here you scaled it into a recurring channel.
- “Improved workflows/editorial coordination” overlaps with the Director role; frame this item as building the foundation rather than leading enterprise governance.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong themes, but this topline item overlaps heavily with the header, Core Competencies, and recent roles. It would be stronger if tightened to distinctive leadership-level capabilities and framed with sharper, less generic wording.

Suggested edit:
- Replace broad phrases with more specific, senior-level language:
- Enterprise digital strategy and communications operations
- Editorial governance, publishing standards, and content workflows
- Cross-channel campaign leadership across web, email, social, and video
- Public-sector and advocacy communications strategy
- Audience-centered content planning and information design
- Consider reducing to 4 bullets to improve scannability and avoid repeating “leadership/strategy” language already used elsewhere.
- If space allows, align wording to recent impact areas from 2022–present, especially governance, enterprise web improvement, and campaign platforms.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy” and “Editorial systems and governance” duplicate Core Competencies almost verbatim.
- “Multi-channel communications leadership” repeats language already demonstrated in the Director of Digital Media entry.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems

items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster, but it reads as a generic tool list and overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” section. In Topline Skills, this should emphasize higher-value, recent capabilities tied to modernization and delivery rather than repeat every platform.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tool inventory to capability-led phrasing: “Drupal and enterprise CMS modernization • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript, jQuery) • API integrations and workflow automation • Airtable-based operational systems • AI-enabled search experiences”
- Put the most marketable/recent items first: Drupal, CMS modernization, AI-enabled search, integrations/automation.
- Remove lower-signal or older items from this topline section if not central to current targeting; keep SharePoint/Power Pages in “Technical + IT” instead.
- If space allows, sharpen with scope language: “enterprise CMS modernization” or “public-sector web platforms” to align with recent experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Drupal,” “WordPress,” “SharePoint,” and “Power Pages” are already repeated in Technical + IT.
- “AI-enabled search experiences” also appears in Core Competencies and the header summary.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant tools list, but it reads as a generic inventory rather than a senior-level capability statement. It also overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” analytics section, so this version should emphasize strategic application over tool repetition.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools-only to capability-led phrasing, e.g. “Analytics strategy, reporting & optimization.”
- Tighten and group items: “GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI, Microsoft Clarity”
- Replace generic terms with higher-value language: “KPI framework design” instead of “KPI design”; “executive reporting” instead of “leadership reporting”
- Consider revised line: “Analytics strategy & optimization • GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI, Microsoft Clarity • KPI framework design • Executive reporting • SEO and performance analysis”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates “Data, Analytics & Optimization” in Technical + IT; keep Topline Skills more strategic and leave the full tool list below.
- “Analytics and reporting infrastructure” already appears in Core Competencies, so avoid repeating that exact phrasing.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery
items.content:
- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong skill cluster, but it overlaps with both Core Competencies (“Multimedia production and livestream operations”) and multiple NACo bullets. Tighten it to emphasize higher-value, current capabilities rather than generic production tasks.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe toward leadership + delivery, not just tools: “Broadcast-quality video production • Livestream and hybrid event delivery • In-house studio operations • PTZ camera and multi-camera workflows”
- Replace “Video production and editing” with a more senior phrase like “Broadcast-quality video production” or “End-to-end video production” to better match Director-level experience.
- Consider swapping “Hybrid and virtual event production” for “Hybrid event production and livestream operations” to align with wording already supported by recent roles.
- If space allows, add scale/context instead of a generic tool item, e.g. “Studio buildout and live event production” given the NACo in-house studio achievement.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Livestreaming” and “Hybrid and virtual event production” are partially redundant; combine them.
- This section overlaps with Core Competencies and Technical + IT; avoid repeating tool-level detail already covered there.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it reads as a generic inventory and overlaps heavily with “Topline Skills.” Use this space to sharpen relevance and signal depth in the platforms most tied to recent work, especially Drupal.

Suggested edit:
- Reorder by relevance/recency: **Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages**
- Add proficiency framing instead of a bare list, e.g.: **Drupal (enterprise migration, microsites, modular content) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages**
- If space allows, make it outcomes-oriented: **Drupal (10,000+ page migration; microsite and toolkit builds) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages**
- Consider dropping **GitHub Pages** unless it reflects meaningful recent use; it is less strategic than the other platforms and may dilute seniority.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item substantially duplicates **Topline Skills → Web Platforms & Technical Execution**; avoid repeating the same platform list in both places.
- “Web & CMS administration” already appears in Core Competencies, so this section should add specificity, not restate categories.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical stack, but it reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution.” Tighten it to emphasize implementation tools that support recent Drupal, analytics, automation, and AI/search work.

Suggested edit:
- Rename/refocus to: **Front-End & Technical Implementation**
- Rewrite as: **HTML5/CSS3 • JavaScript/jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions**
- Drop version numbers unless required by the role; “HTML/CSS/JavaScript” is cleaner and more current.
- If accurate, add one higher-impact qualifier in parentheses or adjacent context elsewhere, e.g. **API integrations (analytics, CMS, search)** or **GitHub Actions (deployment/workflow automation)**.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This duplicates “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” and “API integrations” already listed under Topline Skills; keep the stronger version in one place.
- “Cloudflare Workers” and “GitHub Actions” are the most distinctive items here—retain them if space is tight.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this reads as a generic software list rather than evidence of workflow systems leadership. Since “workflow automation” already appears in Core Competencies and Topline Skills, this item should be tighter and more clearly differentiated.

Suggested edit:
- Split by function to show intent, not just tools: “Automation: Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier | Work management: Jira, Asana, Trello, Basecamp | Collaboration: Slack, Teams”
- Remove weaker/older tools unless they are current and used recently; prioritize Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier, Jira, Asana, Slack, Teams.
- If space allows, add a light qualifier for impact: “used to build cross-team workflows, approvals, and reporting processes.”
- Consider renaming to “Workflow Automation & Collaboration Tools” for clearer alignment with recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Airtable systems” and “Workflow automation” already appear in Topline Skills; avoid repeating the same wording here.
- Slack/Teams are common collaboration tools and may add little value unless central to your systems work.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The item is clear but too bare relative to the rest of the CV. Since email leadership already appears in recent NACo roles, this line should stay tool-focused and avoid restating channel ownership.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Email Marketing & Member Engagement Platforms**
- Tighten platform names for readability: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights – Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp**
- If accurate, add capability keywords instead of more tools: **campaign automation, newsletter operations, audience segmentation, journey orchestration**
- Best combined version: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights – Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp • campaign automation • audience segmentation**

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Avoid adding claims like “managed newsletters” or “led email strategy” here; those are already covered in Work Experience.
- If Dynamics 365/ Higher Logic were not used recently or materially, consider dropping the least relevant platform to keep this section aligned with your strongest recent experience.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid progression story, but this reads broadly and overlaps with the stronger 2018–2024 NACo entries. Make it more foundational and execution-focused, with concrete outputs and team-building impact.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe as early-stage buildout: “Promoted across two digital roles to help launch NACo’s first in-house digital team and formalize workflows across web, email, social and multimedia.”
- Add measurable scope where possible: website refresh size/traffic, number of livestreams or weekly videos produced, audience reach, or frequency/volume of content.
- Tighten phrasing and emphasize hands-on delivery: “Supported a major website refresh, produced recurring livestreams and weekly video updates, and coached a digital media associate on daily production and publishing.”
- If metrics are unavailable, swap “high-impact” for specifics like “recurring,” “organization-wide,” or “member-facing.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 role; position this item as launching or establishing the format rather than expanding it.
- “Strengthening workflows” repeats later governance/operations themes; keep this version tactical and foundational.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry with a credible “first podcast” achievement, but it reads broadly and overlaps with later NACo roles in digital content and multimedia. Emphasize the distinct innovation/research scope and make the podcast launch the clearest outcome.

Suggested edit:
- Lead with the differentiator: “Coordinated county innovation and research initiatives supporting NACo programs and policy priorities.”
- Tighten the digital piece: “Produced digital and multimedia content to translate research and program work into member-facing communications.”
- Make the podcast accomplishment sharper: “Launched NACo’s first podcast, leading concept development, episode planning, scripting, and production.”
- If possible, add scope or output metrics: number of projects supported, episodes produced, audiences reached, or teams/stakeholders coordinated.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Avoid generic “digital content production and multimedia materials” phrasing; later roles already cover multimedia extensively.
- Don’t overstate leadership in digital operations here, since stronger team/platform leadership appears in 2015–2024 roles.
